about.title: Richmond Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Richmond comes without warning, the paperwork arrives faster than the grief settles. Public crash records for this Contra Costa County city show eight traffic deaths in 2025, alongside 453 injury collisions that hurt 618 people. Many of those crashes clustered along I-80, Richmond Parkway, Barrett Avenue and I-580, and reports tended to peak on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Behind each number is a household missing a paycheck, a parent, or a partner. California law lets certain surviving family members bring a civil wrongful death action, separate from any criminal charges the district attorney may or may not pursue. That claim can seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for lost love, companionship and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Richmond families, at no charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Richmond Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Sort Out Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can confirm where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: We Respect the Clock
items.desc: Most Richmond wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but the window is much shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Early contact keeps those options open.

items.title: Nothing Owed Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Our connection service is free, and network attorneys work on contingency. Your family pays no attorney fee unless the case results in a recovery.

items.question: The crash that killed my father on Richmond Parkway involved a city vehicle. Does that change the deadline?
items.answer: Yes, it usually does. When a government entity such as the City of Richmond, Contra Costa County or Caltrans may be responsible, a formal claim generally has to be presented within months, not years, before any lawsuit can be filed. Missing that step can end the case before it starts, so it is worth speaking with an attorney quickly.

items.question: The driver is being prosecuted in Contra Costa County. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death action is a civil case brought by the family, and it runs on its own track from any criminal prosecution. The two can move at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other. An attorney can explain how evidence from the criminal matter may still be useful.

items.question: What losses can our family actually recover in a Richmond wrongful death case?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have contributed over their lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship, comfort and guidance. Each family's situation is different, and no attorney can promise a particular result. The independent attorney you are connected with will review the specifics and set honest expectations.
